newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals open lower but covering seen.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals open lower but covering seen.

text.p: New York precious metals futures opened lower as expected Friday but key support levels held as funds began shortcovering ahead of the end of the third quarter, traders said.

"Spot gold bullion dipped just below the key $380.00 support level, but buying by the trade, the banks and the arb funds then came in and funds are beginning to square up, cover shorts and book profits ahead of the end of quarter," Pell Brothers floor trader Don Tierney said.
COMEX December gold was down $0.60 at $383.00 an ounce, up from an early low of $381.90.

In New York bullion trade, spot gold was quoted around $380.50 after dipping to a session low during the first hour of trade of $379.70 versus a London morning fix Friday of $380.30 and New York close Thursday around $381.10.
Key support at $380 that has held since early 1995 is still seen under threat next week though, traders said.

"The latest rumor to hit this increasingly thin market was that some European Union members would dispose of their gold holdings, using the proceeds to reduce their deficit to GDP ratio to within the Maastricht guidelines for acceptance into the single currency," CPM Group analyst Edward Kempf said.

"The rumor seemed farfetched to say the least as the size of the debts of most of these countries exceeds the value of their gold holdings by a wide margin, meaning the exercise would be meaningless," he said. "Gold is clearly susceptible to further short selling, with a longer term target of $374."
One-month implied gold lease rates have been moving up, suggesting fresh short selling, analysts said.

Official gold sales were also a concern Thursday after IMF head Michel Camdessus said the IMF now had the needed 85 percent majority in favor of the plan to sell about five million ounces of its 104 million ounce reserve to help fund third world debt relief, but U.S. Treasury Secretary Rubin said the sales may not be needed until the year 2000.

Precious metals futures have been in a downtrend for the past three weeks, largely driven by fund selling, with investor demand low due to healthy U.S. stock and bond markets and low U.S. inflation, analysts said.
COMEX December silver was up 0.5 cent at $4.890.
NYMEX October platinum was down $1.30 at $386.50 after setting a contract low of $385.50.
NYMEX December palladium was unchanged at $119.00.
-Clive McKeef, New York Commodities Desk, +1-212-859-1641 email: clive.mckeef@reuters.com
